title: SCIM progressive suspend flow with TTL, audit bindings, and controlled retry gates
creator: Noah Kim
description: Background: Customers report accidental user deletions via SCIM and demand stronger auditability and a configurable grace period before irreversible deletes. Current SCIM handlers retry aggressively on transient failures and sometimes re-play patch sequences that remove group memberships before user suspension is recorded in audit logs. This ticket implements a progressive suspend (soft-deprovision) flow: on SCIM RemoveUser/Delete operations we first mark users as 'suspended' with a tenant-configurable TTL, emit a rich audit event, and only perform final deletion after TTL expires and background checks pass. The flow must be idempotent, observable, and allow tenant admins to opt into immediate deletes via RBAC v2 privileges.
goals: Introduce a staged deprovision state (suspended_until + suspended_by) surfaced via SCIM extensions
Ensure every suspend/unsuspend/terminate action writes a single audit record containing actor, reason, trace_id, and pre/post deltas
Replace current retry pattern with controlled retry gates (bounded exponential backoff + tenant windows) to reduce double-applies
Enable per-tenant policy: suspend TTL, max retry attempts, immediate-delete roles (RBAC v2)
non_goals: Changing SCIM schema version globally (we will use SCIM extension attributes)
Full bulk-import redesign (follow-up bulk-optimizations ticket will be created)
proposal_summary: 1) On SCIM delete/Remove: translate to internal state transition USER -> SUSPENDED with suspended_until = now + tenant.ttl and record suspended_by/scim_request_id. 2) Emit Audit event (type=scim.suspend) with the SCIM patch payload, actor, tenant id, and trace_id. 3) Enqueue a background termination job scheduled at suspended_until. The job re-checks: user reactivation, outstanding org policies, open sessions, and group membership or service-account dependencies. 4) If final delete is allowed and RBAC v2 permits, perform delete; else keep suspended but mark as 'deletion_blocked' with audit note. 5) Retry gate: use exponential backoff with cap and jitter for transient SCIM upstream 5xx; persist last_attempt_at and attempt_count into a lightweight retry table to avoid replays across service restarts.
implementation_notes: DB: add user.suspended_until (timestamp), user.suspended_by_scim (string), user.suspension_reason (string), retry_state table with (scim_request_id, last_attempt_at, attempts, next_backoff_at)
SCIM: expose suspended_until via enterprise extension urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User as 'x-redwood-suspendedUntil'
Audit: new audit types scim.suspend, scim.terminate, scim.retry_fail and consistent trace_id propagation through request middleware
RBAC v2: add permission 'users.immediate_delete' that bypasses TTL and allows admin-triggered finalize-delete endpoints
Retries: bounded exponential backoff (base=2s, cap=30m), jitter, and tenant-configurable max_attempts (default 6)
Idempotency: use scim_request_id (X-SCIM-Request-Id) for dedupe of delete/patch operations; PATCH ops must be applied idempotently
Groups: ensure group-membership removals are applied in the same suspended transaction or deferred until finalize-delete to avoid inconsistent resource access claims
Rate limits: for tenants doing bulk deprovisions, run finalize-delete in batched worker windows to respect cluster QPS and avoid broad throttles
acceptance_criteria: New suspended state visible via SCIM GET /Users with x-redwood-suspendedUntil on suspended accounts
Suspending a user produces exactly one scim.suspend audit entry with trace_id and payload link
Final delete only occurs after TTL expiration unless actor has users.immediate_delete permission
Retry behavior persists across service restarts and adheres to tenant max_attempts
E2E tests cover SCIM delete -> suspend -> reactivate before TTL -> no final delete
Dashboards show retry_attempts, suspend_to_delete lag, and suspended user counts per-tenant
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind tenant flag 'scim.progressive_deprovision' - default off for existing tenants
Canary rollout: enable for 10 internal tenants, monitor for 72 hours, then expand to 100 tenants
Provide a tenant admin console toggle to shorten TTL for emergency cleanup
Phased docs and migration guide (Confluence) + communication to customer success
test_plan: Unit: retry gate logic, backoff math, idempotency key handling
Integration: SCIM delete request -> DB suspended_until set -> background job fired -> if reactivated within TTL job aborts
Load: simulate 50k user suspends across tenants and verify worker batching and finalizer backpressure
Security: RBAC unit/integ tests to confirm only users.immediate_delete can finalize early
known_risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Suspended users may still hold cached tokens - Mitigation: trigger session revocation at suspend time and record in audit
Risk: Bulk deletes overload finalize workers - Mitigation: adaptive batching and tenant throttling with exponential cool-down
Risk: Customer confusion about 'suspended' vs 'deleted' - Mitigation: UX copy in Console and SCIM docs + email templates from CSM
